notes.text:
Draft theorem. Let C be complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued of characteristic and residue characteristic zero, X/C the given smooth geometrically integral projective curve of any genus, and L its actual ample rational line bundle. For any finite prescribed type-II set, the construction gives an actual proper strongly semistable formal model of X^an and an actual formal bundle A with specified generic identification A_eta=kdL. Its degree is strictly positive on every component of the final special fibre, and its whole reduction modulo a is relatively ample. This is an unverified draft relative to ordinary sources, not an accepted equation theorem.

Horizontal proof. Set R=C-circle and R_j=R/a^j for 0<|a|<1. The maximal ideal modulo a^j is nil, possibly without a uniform nilpotence exponent; Spec R_j has one point. In an actual smooth étale formal coordinate chart B, the given bounded C-point p evaluates restricted series convergently, giving B->R and compatible evaluations for ALL j. Put b=t(p), and remove other residual roots so the residual zero fibre of t-b is one reduced point. E_j=(B/a^j)/(t-b) is étale affine over R_j and evaluation is a retraction. An étale section is an open immersion by base change of the open diagonal; affine separatedness also makes it closed. The extended nil ideal does not change points, so E_j has one point. The section has full open image, hence E_j=R_j including its structure sheaf. This uses the given section, rather than a residue-cardinality inference.

The monic parameter t-b is regular on R_j[t], its localization and the flat étale chart B/a^j. Separation makes it regular on B. If f evaluates to zero, there are unique q_j satisfying f=(t-b)q_j modulo a^j. Uniqueness makes them compatible; completeness gives q and f=(t-b)q. Thus the evaluation kernel is exactly the closed regular principal ideal (t-b), B/(t-b)=R, its generic quotient is the original C-point, and its residual intersection has multiplicity one. On overlaps identical section ideals have unit-related regular generators and glue with the unit ideal off their residual image.

Actual application. Choose the original very ample integral M=dL and nonzero original section S0, with divisor sum n_p p and D=deg M>0. If starting over K, choose d and S0 over K before extension and retain those pullbacks over C. Whole BPR v1 4.22, 3.13, 3.14 and 4.11/4.15 supply the actual marked model of the given curve. Marks have distinct smooth reductions by 4.8. The étale standard charts in 4.4 restrict at a smooth point to a unit-coordinate formal multiplicative line. Bounded evaluation and residual localization satisfy the preceding hypotheses. Consequently H=sum n_p H_p gives O(H)_eta=M via this S0. Its component degrees a_v are nonnegative integers summing to D.

Keep the entire connected graph, with lengths in Gamma=-log|C*|, a nonzero divisible dense subgroup. Choose q_v>0 summing to D and solve Delta_out h=q-a. The negative weighted graph matrix is symmetric, has constants as kernel by its edge-square identity, and has exactly the zero-sum image. Approximate shared global heights by g_v in Gamma. On an edge of length ell, strictly bracket s=(g_w-g_v)/ell by nearby rationals p<s<r. The bend t=(r ell-(g_w-g_v))/(r-p) belongs to Gamma and satisfies 0<t<ell. Slopes p then r reach the exact shared heights and give positive bend degree r-p. Outgoing-slope errors below min(q)/(4 maximum valence) preserve positive old degrees. Every final old and new component is checked; loops count twice and every cycle survives subdivision.

Clear slopes by k and choose c_v with -log|c_v|=k g_v. On the actual oriented node xy=b_e use c_v x^m. Ratios to vertex factors are x^m and (c_v b_e^m/c_w)y^(-m). The endpoint identity gives scalar norm one, hence an R-unit, without requiring literal scalar equality. Flatness makes x,y and nonzero scalars regular meromorphic factors. These unit ratios glue a genuine vertical Cartier divisor, including around cycles. In frames f^(-1), section 1 has weight -log|f|, exactly k g composed with the actual retraction. The relation e_v=x^m e_e gives degree +m on the first component and -m on the second. Thus A=O(H)^k tensor O(V_g) has old degrees k(a_v+Delta_out g(v))>0 and bend degrees k(r-p)>0, summing to kD. Its generic bundle remains M^k. Divide the entire weight by kd to obtain a metric on L, with raw degree D/d=deg L; its scalar change from the horizontal M/d metric is g/d.

The actual proper formal model has proper scheme reductions by formal properness. BPR admissible charts have finitely generated ideals and flatness, so their reductions are locally fp; the finite separated cover gives fp. Whole Stacks33.44.15/14 applies positive degree on every component only on the proper FIELD residue curve. General37.50.3,0D2S then gives relative ampleness near the sole point of Spec(R/a), hence on the entire base. No Noetherian theorem is applied directly to R/a and no bounded nilpotence is assumed.

notes.text:
Draft field lemma. Suppose reduced strict C-affinoid B has every nonzero spectral norm in |C*| and canonical reduction Btilde a domain. Normalize f,g by scalars of their exact norms. Their nonzero reductions have nonzero product, so the product norm is one. Scaling proves spectral multiplicativity and zero kernel, defining an actual analytic point x reducing generically. Every generic-reduction point evaluates normalized nonzero f/c with norm one, hence evaluates every f by the spectral norm. Uniqueness follows from these hypotheses; it is not a premise about residue fields.

H(x) completes honest Frac(B). For h of norm<=1, approximate by f/g with error<1. Then |f/g|<=1. Choose c with |c|=||g||. Both f/c and g/c are powerbounded, the latter has nonzero reduction, and the residue of h is their residual fraction. Thus H(x)-residue=Frac(Btilde), covering the entire residue field rather than a coordinate subfield.

Actual application. BPR4.14/4.15 gives the canonical affinoid U_v=retraction^(-1)(v) when the graph has edges, with singleton SHILOV boundary the actual type-II vertex and canonical reduction an affine open of the same component. In the edgeless case use the complement of one open ball from4.12/4.15.3. Type II gives rational rank zero of the value-group quotient. Every real value has an integer multiple in the divisible base group, so no new values occur. Every nonzero analytic function attains its spectral norm at the actual Shilov vertex, hence in |C*|. Smooth generic reducedness gives faithfulness. The canonical reduction is a domain. These facts verify the lemma’s hypotheses and prove H(v)-residue=kappa(C_v). This uses more than BPR4.6’s singleton reduction fibre and does not use R-flatness as parameter injection or working254 as a grant.

For n2’s actual integral A, whole CLDv1 6.5.1/6.6.8 identifies its residual bundle by the exact norm-one formal transition cocycle with A|C_v. Whole field equality makes C_v a model, not a premodel with an unknown extension factor. The original analytic curve is good, separated, smooth, pure one-dimensional and boundaryless. Nongeneric reduction closures are zero-dimensional; 6.9.2 through6.8.3 kills their curvature. Positive degree rules out definition dimension zero at a vertex. Literal AC6.9.4, including the entire calibrated-cone proof6.9.5, gives coefficient deg(A|C_v). The value-group factor is one, and primitive/residue calibration multiplicities are accounted for by that theorem. No probability normalization, factorial or general stable-field shortcut is applied; the v1 exponent omission is harmless only in this n=1 scope.

Consequently the actual locally approachable PL metric phi_g has genuine CLD first Chern measure sum_v deg(A|C_v)/(kd) delta_v. All coefficients are positive, and actual Cartier cancellation gives raw total kD/(kd)=deg L. Local PL approachability uses the source’s residual difference-of-generated-bundles construction. At every analytic point integral coefficients have norms<=1, while 1=sum b_i f_i forces max |f_i|=1.
